subject: EdgeCloud.ai - post-demo differentiator checklist & unit-econ asks
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Torres <elena@edgecloud.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: EdgeCloud.ai - post-demo differentiator checklist & unit-econ asks

Hi Elena — thanks again for carving out time for the demo today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we don't lose momentum.

Recap (30-min demo highlights):
- You saw a live chat flow using our 7B quantized model with 120ms median generator latency (demo infra) and streaming tokens to the client.
- We showed automatic prefix caching reduced token generation in the demo by ~22% for repeated prompts (demo data).
- We highlighted routing policies: fall back to lower-cost variant (4-bit) when Dedicated pool is saturated.

Open qualification questions (we need these to calibrate unit-econ and the next tests):
1) Typical concurrent qps for your user-facing assistant (p90 request size and target latency)?
2) Production cache hit expectations for templated prompts vs. open user input (ballpark %)?
3) Priority: lowest per-token cost or strict 99th-latency SLO? Any hard SLA targets?

Proposed next tests (what we can run in a week):
- 1M-token synthetic run using your sample prompt mix to estimate per-1M token cost across: Redwood Hosted, Redwood Dedicated, and their equivalent on Hyperscaler-A managed endpoints.
- Sensitivity matrix: batch-size vs latency (1, 4, 8) and cache-hit levels (0%, 20%, 50%).
- Model variant delta: 7B q4 vs 13B q4 -> quality/latency/econ breakpoints.

Attachments: 
- edge-econ-1m-token-model-matrix.xlsx (worked example + params we used in demo)
- 20260920-demo-screenshots.pdf (UI + trace snippets)

Ask: If you can confirm the three qualification inputs above by EOD Wednesday we’ll schedule the 1M-token run and invite your infra lead to a quick 30-min sync.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Account Exec | Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0126

From: Elena Torres <elena@edgecloud.ai>

Cc: procure@edgecloud.ai
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2026 09:32:00 -0400
Subject: Re: EdgeCloud.ai - post-demo differentiator checklist & unit-econ asks

Thanks Mina — great session. Quick answers below, and a couple of asks from procurement.

Answers:
- Concurrent QPS: avg 45 qps, peak 180 qps during morning batch jobs. Typical user prompt median tokens ~120, p95 ~450.
- Cache hit expectation: for system prompts and templated flows we expect ~35% hit on first pass, increasing to ~50% with user segmentation and prefix normalization.
- SLA: target p95 latency < 350ms for interactive flows; 99th not yet hardened but we'd prefer to avoid >1s tails.

Procurement asks:
- Can you provide a short per-1M token comparison vs "Hyperscaler-A Managed" for the 7B q4 and 13B q4 variants (including egress/req overhead assumptions)?
- We'd like to see any standard MSA redline items in advance (NDA/PSL/SLAs).

Happy to sync with the infra lead — cc'd procurement for timeline alignment. Scheduling note: I’m on travel Wed afternoon but free Thu morning.

Best,
Elena
Head of Product | EdgeCloud.ai

(Forwarded for internal review to procure@edgecloud.ai)
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Torres <elena@edgecloud.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, procure@edgecloud.ai
Date: Wed, 22 Sep 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: EdgeCloud.ai - post-demo differentiator checklist & unit-econ asks

Elena — thanks for the quick clarification, that data is very helpful. Below I’m attaching a concise cost comparison and an initial plan for the 1M-token runs. Ben and Jonas added technical notes inline.

High-level per-1M token comparison (ballpark, USD):
- Redwood Hosted (7B q4) — $68 per 1M tokens (includes token compute + network overhead as configured in our sample run)
- Redwood Dedicated reserved pricing (7B q4, medium tier) — $40 per 1M tokens (amortized on typical 3mo commit)
- Hyperscaler-A managed endpoint (7B q4-equivalent) — $95 per 1M tokens (their public list + extra egress assumptions)

Notes and assumptions: Jonas: we assumed 35% prefix cache hit; batch size 4; median output length 120 tokens; routing overhead 3%. See attached matrix for full model/quantization rows.

Ben (tech note): Redwood advantage is twofold for you: 1) predictable Dedicated reserving that reduces unit cost when you commit, and 2) smarter prefix/KV caching that reduces tokens sent to model for templated flows — both matter with your ~35% baseline cache hit. Hyperscaler-A has better single-node latency in some configs but charges per-request and doesn't expose prefix/KV caching at the layer we can instrument.

Proposed execution plan for the 1M-token run:
- We will run three parallel experiments over the next 72 hours: Hosted 7B q4, Dedicated 7B q4 (burst disabled), Hyperscaler-A emulation (using their published perf numbers and a small synthetic run to validate).
- We'll capture: per-token $ estimate, p50/p95/p99 latencies, batch hit/signal, effective cache-hit impact (tokens saved), and a quality sample of 200 responses for your team to review.

Procurement / Legal: I’m attaching our standard MSA + a short summary of SLAs we offer for Dedicated customers. If there are specific redlines please mark them and we’ll triage quickly.

Next step: Jonas to coordinate infra specifics with your infra lead and schedule the 30-min sync. Thur morning works for Mina to run through results on the call.

Thanks,
Mina

---
Attachments: edge-econ-1m-token-model-matrix.xlsx (updated), 20260922-redwood-msa-dedicated-summary.pdf

Jonas Weber technical note:
- We will instrument token-level tracing to capture KV cache hits per request; please provide a representative sample of 500 prompts (anonymized) to seed the run.

Ben Carter brief:
- If you want, we can also run quantization sensitivity (7B q4 -> 7B q8) to show where quality and latency trade off; typically q8 gives a tiny latency win but larger quality delta depending on model family.

Thanks everyone — looking forward to the run.

Elena
